dataset_family: BABRI (Beijing Aging Brain Rejuvenation Initiative) community cohort, Beijing Normal University; MRI at the BNU Imaging Center for Brain Research, 18F-florbetapir PET; single cohort, not public
method_family: Atlas-based single-shell DTI (FA/MD over 20 JHU tracts, PANDA, ROI ANCOVA) set against whole-brain SPM12 voxel-based morphometry of grey-matter volume; florbetapir PET visual read for amyloid grouping
what_it_shows: Dai et al. 2026, Front Neurol 16:1658712 (BABRI, Beijing; 19 amyloid-negative MCI, 18 amyloid-positive MCI, 32 NC, no age/sex/education differences). In amyloid-negative MCI vs NC, atlas-ROI DTI separates the groups (lower FA in cingulum CCG/CH, ILF, IFOF, UF, forceps minor and others; higher MD in many tracts) while whole-brain VBM finds no grey-matter atrophy surviving FWE correction ('atrophy trend ... did not reach statistical significance'). In amyloid-positive MCI both DTI and VBM (bilateral hippocampal and left parahippocampal atrophy) separate from NC, so there is no dissociation in that arm. The authors state the white-matter-before-grey-matter pattern themselves.
why: Identity: PDF title, authors (Dai X, Zhang J, ... Peng D, Zhang Z) and DOI 10.3389/fneur.2025.1658712 match the block; extract read in full to the References. PART SHOWN: a within-study, same-participant head-to-head in which a diffusion-microstructure measure separates an MCI group from a matched non-impaired comparator where a macrostructural volume measure does not; this is the diffusion limb of the Table A1 form, in amyloid-negative MCI only. WHY NOT YES: (1) It holds only in the amyloid-negative subgroup (n=19), which the authors describe as a heterogeneous population that may carry non-AD pathology; in amyloid-positive MCI VBM also separated (bilateral hippocampus), and MCI as a whole was never compared with NC, so the study does not show that the static measure fails for MCI in general. (2) The static measure does not correspond to the same structure: white-matter tract diffusion is set against voxelwise grey-matter volume. No white-matter volume is analysed, and no hippocampal-volume ROI test for amyloid-negative MCI vs NC is reported (the left-CH MD / left-HIP GMV pairing appears only in the all-participant mediation model). (3) The two arms were tested at different stringency: VBM at voxelwise p<0.001 uncorrected, then whole-brain FWE p<0.05, against ANCOVA on 20 atlas ROIs with FDR (Methods) or Bonferroni (Figure 2 caption, an internal inconsistency). The VBM result is a threshold null ('trend'), not a demonstrated absence, and the less stringent ROI test favours the diffusion arm. (4) Pairwise DTI statistics are given only as Figure 2 superscripts and in Supplementary Table S2, with no effect sizes in the text. (5) There is no measure-by-group interaction test. (6) The design is cross-sectional and not every NC had PET. INDEPENDENCE: BABRI, Beijing. It shares no cohort, site or author with P-651 (Chongqing; Li B. et al.), P-661 (Illinois/UT Dallas/UTSW; Lydon et al.), P-662 (Shanghai; Xiao et al.), P-665/P-687 (Guangzhou; Zhang S./Cheng X. et al.) or P-666 (Wuhan Tongji; Shao et al.), and none with the other candidates. METHOD FAMILY CAVEAT: DTI tensor FA/MD with atlas ROIs is the same method family as current supporter P-666 (64-direction DTI, TBSS plus ICBM atlas ROI), which round 20 scored 'no'. It is distinct from P-651's multi-shell NODDI. BABRI is also the dataset of P-981, a previously rejected VF-25 supporter; that is a different study, and its rejection has no bearing here. Not a registry duplicate stub. Peer-reviewed, not a preprint. NARROWED: the packet says the record is not a convergence, so n/a.

Our results showed significant multidomain cognitive decline and extensive disruptions of WM integrity in both Aβneg and Aβpos MCI subgroups, with significant hippocampal atrophy observed only in Aβpos MCI group.

This study found significant WM damage in both Aβpos and Aβneg MCI groups, while notable GM atrophy was only observed in the Aβpos MCI group.
